title: Plan the launch week
recap: Pipo planned your launch week, day by day.
funFact: A clear plan is where agents shine: they keep every date, budget and person in mind at once. Next, Pipo emails your designer for you!
postcard: a neon-lit night city shop window with hand-poured candles and a big launch-week planner on the wall: {answer}
situation: Big week! Ember & Oak's online shop is about to open. Want me to plan the days before?
facts: 💸 $300 for ads, and not a cent more
📸 Maya does photos and posts, but she's off Wednesday
🎯 Goal: 50 orders in the first week
systemPrompt: You are Pipo, a friendly personal assistant for the founder of a small online business. Help with what they ask. Keep it short: one line per point.

slots.label: What do you want Pipo to do?

pieces.label: Get our online shop ready to open
pieces.text: Help me get Ember & Oak, my small candle brand, ready to open its online shop.

pieces.label: Help me launch my business
pieces.text: Help me launch my business and get lots of sales.

slots.label: What does Pipo need to know?

pieces.label: We open Friday, December 4
pieces.text: The shop opens on Friday, December 4.

pieces.label: $300 for ads, no more
pieces.text: We have $300 to spend on ads, and no more.

pieces.label: Maya does photos and posts, off Wednesday
pieces.text: My cofounder Maya does the photos and social posts, but she's off on Wednesday.

pieces.label: Make it go viral!
pieces.tip: "Go viral" is a wish, not a plan. Facts like dates, money and people give Pipo something to plan around.

slots.label: What counts as a good launch?

pieces.label: 50 orders in the first week
pieces.text: Our goal is 50 orders in the first week.

pieces.label: As many sales as possible
pieces.text: Get as many sales as possible.
pieces.tip: "As many as possible" can't be planned for. A number gives Pipo a target to plan toward.

pieces.label: A day-by-day plan with who does what
pieces.text: Give me a plan with one line per day, Monday to Friday, saying who does what.

pieces.label: Lots of marketing ideas
pieces.text: Give me lots of marketing ideas.
pieces.tip: A pile of ideas still leaves the planning to you. Ask for the shape you can act on.

flaws.hint: "Help me launch my business" doesn't say what the business is or what to plan.
flaws.explain: Pipo didn't know you sell candles, so the plan could be for any business.

flaws.hint: You didn't tell Pipo when the shop opens.
flaws.explain: Pipo didn't know you open Friday, December 4, so the plan doesn't build up to launch day.

flaws.hint: You didn't tell Pipo your ad budget.
flaws.explain: Pipo didn't know you have $300 for ads, so the plan doesn't keep spending in check.

flaws.hint: You didn't tell Pipo about Maya.
flaws.explain: Pipo didn't know Maya does the photos and is off Wednesday, so nobody is clearly in charge of them.

flaws.hint: "As many sales as possible" doesn't give Pipo a target.
flaws.explain: Pipo didn't know your goal is 50 orders, so the plan has nothing to aim for.

flaws.hint: "Lots of marketing ideas" doesn't say what kind of answer you need.
flaws.explain: Pipo gave you ideas, not a plan, so you still have to work out what happens each day.

lesson: For a bigger job, give Pipo every fact that matters, a clear goal and the shape of the answer you need.
